# INA Platform — Setup Guide

This adds a real, functional layer to the site: visitors can create an account,
submit a digital infrastructure project, attach supporting documents, and get
back an **Investment Readiness Index™** score (0–100 across 8 dimensions) plus
**Multilateral Finance Navigator™** recommendations — generated by Claude
against INA's own documented framework methodology (see `framework.html`,
sections F2 and F6).

New pages: `register.html`, `login.html`, `dashboard.html`, `new-project.html`,
`project.html`. Entry point: the **Platform** page now has a "Get Started" /
"Sign in" section.

This needs two pieces of infrastructure you don't have yet: a **Supabase**
project (database + authentication + file storage) and some **environment
variables** in your existing Vercel project. Both are free to start. Total
setup time: about 15–20 minutes.

---

## 1. Create a Supabase project

1. Go to https://supabase.com → Sign up (or log in) → **New Project**.
2. Pick any name/region, set a database password (save it somewhere), and wait
   ~2 minutes for it to provision.
3. Once ready, go to **Project Settings → API**. You'll need three values from
   this page in the steps below:
   - **Project URL** (e.g. `https://abcdefgh.supabase.co`)
   - **anon / public key**
   - **service_role key** (click "Reveal" — keep this one secret, never put it
     in frontend code)

## 2. Run the database schema

1. In Supabase, go to **SQL Editor → New query**.
2. Open `supabase/schema.sql` (in this same folder), copy its entire contents,
   paste into the query editor, and click **Run**.
3. This creates the `profiles`, `projects`, `project_documents` and
   `framework_analysis` tables, with security rules so each user can only see
   their own data.

## 3. Create the storage bucket

1. In Supabase, go to **Storage → Create a new bucket**.
2. Name it exactly: `project-documents`
3. Set **Public bucket: OFF** (keep it private — the schema.sql policies
   already grant each user access to their own folder inside it).
4. Click **Create bucket**. (The access policies for this bucket were already
   created by `schema.sql` in step 2 — nothing else to configure here.)

## 4. Configure the frontend (Supabase URL + anon key)

1. Open `assets/platform.js` in this project.
2. Near the top, find:
   ```js
   const INA_PLATFORM_CONFIG = {
     SUPABASE_URL: 'YOUR_SUPABASE_URL',
     SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: 'YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY',
   };
   ```
3. Replace both placeholder values with the **Project URL** and **anon/public
   key** from step 1. (This key is safe to put in frontend code — it's
   designed to be public. The database rules from `schema.sql` are what
   actually protect the data.)
4. Save the file.

## 5. Configure the backend (Vercel environment variables)

This site already deploys to Vercel from your GitHub repo. The AI analysis
runs in a serverless function at `api/analyze-project.js`, which needs its own
secrets — set these in Vercel, not in any file you commit:

1. Go to https://vercel.com/dashboard → your project → **Settings →
   Environment Variables**.
2. Add each of the following (Production environment, at minimum):

   | Name | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Your Anthropic API key — create one at https://console.anthropic.com → API Keys (requires billing enabled; usage cost for this feature is a few cents per analysis) |
   | `SUPABASE_URL` | Same Project URL from step 1 |
   | `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | The **service_role** key from step 1 (keep secret) |
   | `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | The **anon/public** key from step 1 |
   | `CLAUDE_MODEL` | `claude-sonnet-5` (optional — this is the default if omitted) |

3. Click **Save** for each, then **redeploy** the project (Vercel usually
   prompts you to redeploy after adding env vars — or just push any small
   change to GitHub to trigger a new deploy).

## 6. Push everything to GitHub

Upload the full site folder to your GitHub repo as usual (including the new
`api/` folder, `supabase/` folder, and the updated `assets/` files) — Vercel
will pick up the `api/analyze-project.js` file automatically as a serverless
function, no extra configuration needed.

## 7. Test it

1. Visit your live site → **Platform** → **Get Started**.
2. Create an account (check your email if Supabase asks you to confirm it —
   by default new Supabase projects require email confirmation; you can turn
   this off in **Authentication → Providers → Email → Confirm email**, if you
   want frictionless signups for now).
3. Submit a test project with a real description.
4. Within under a minute you should see a scored Investment Readiness Index™
   with 8 dimension bars, a gap roadmap, and financing recommendations.

---

## How it works (for reference)

- **Auth & data**: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage). Row Level Security
  policies mean each signed-in user can only ever see their own projects,
  documents and analysis results — enforced at the database level, not just
  in the frontend code.
- **Analysis engine**: `api/analyze-project.js`, a Vercel serverless function.
  It verifies the caller's session, fetches the project (and up to 5 attached
  documents — PDFs and images are sent directly to Claude; plain text files
  are inlined; other formats are referenced by filename only), and calls the
  Anthropic Claude API with a system prompt grounded in INA's own F2
  (Investment Readiness Index™) and F6 (Multilateral Finance Navigator™)
  methodology, as documented on `framework.html`. The API key never touches
  the browser.
- **No build step**: everything is still plain HTML/CSS/JS, consistent with
  the rest of the site. The only new thing is the `api/` folder, which Vercel
  runs as serverless functions automatically.

## Known limitations (v1)

- Document parsing is limited to PDF, PNG/JPEG and plain text/Markdown/CSV
  files. Word documents (.docx), Excel files, etc. are listed by filename in
  the analysis prompt but their content isn't extracted yet.
- Email confirmation on signup is on by default in Supabase — decide whether
  you want that friction or not (see step 7 above).
- There's no password-reset flow yet, no admin view across all users'
  projects, and no email notification when an analysis finishes (the results
  page polls automatically while you have it open).
